findings.issue: The sentence gives the review admission prune set as complete and unconditional: "it prunes a row that lacks evidence or scope, sits outside the review target, repeats a known node, or would exceed the depth, fan-out or budget caps." The scope-containment prune only runs when the review config's `reviewTargetType` is `files`; `scopeInsideReviewTarget` returns true for every other target kind, and the review config default is `spec-folder`, so on a default expansive review run no proposal is ever pruned for scope. The listed set also omits the sixth admission check (`cycle`), which prunes with reason `cycle`, and the dangling-parent case that prunes as `relevance`.

evidence.cmd: rg -n "reviewTargetType !== 'files'|isCommitRange\(source.reviewTarget\)" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs; rg -n "defaultTargetType" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/assets/review-mode-contract.yaml; rg -n "reviewTargetType" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/deep-review/assets/deep-review-config.json; rg -n "// 6. cycle|return checkCycle" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs

findings.issue: Same unconditioned prune claim in the claude mirror: "sits outside the review target" is enforced by `scopeInsideReviewTarget` only when `reviewTargetType === 'files'`; the shipped default (`spec-folder`) never prunes a proposal for scope. The list also omits the `cycle` check and the dangling-parent `relevance` prune that close the six-check admission order.

Same unconditioned prune claim in the pi mirror: "sits outside the review target" holds only for a `files` target because `scopeInsideReviewTarget` short-circuits to true for every other target kind, and `spec-folder` is the config default; the sentence also omits the `cycle` admission check and the dangling-parent `relevance` prune.

The research prune list is written as the complete set of admission outcomes but stops at the budget cap. `frontier-admit.cjs` runs six checks in one fixed order — relevance, dedupe, depth, fan-out, budget, cycle — so a row pruned as `cycle` is undocumented, and so is the relevance prune for a `parentId` the node store does not hold.

evidence.cmd: rg -n "relevance, dedupe, depth, fan-out, monotone budget, acyclicity|!nodes.has\(proposal.parentId\)|// 6. cycle|return checkCycle" .skilled/skills/system-deep-loop/runtime/scripts/frontier-admit.cjs
